newsitem.title: UK: EU could import sugar if world prices fall.
newsitem.headline: EU could import sugar if world prices fall.

text.p: Lower world sugar prices could spark off European Union (EU) imports, especially in deficit member states where local market prices are already high, a key EU sugar official said on Thursday.

"We have a general interest in maintaining a preference for European sugar in all regions and it cannot be excluded that we will have imports in the case of lower market prices," Ejner Stendevad told a two-day conference hosted by Agra Europe.
Stendevad is head of sugar at the EU's Directorate General for Agriculture.
Such imports would weigh on regional premiums for sugar, he said, adding that areas with high prices would be the likely candidates for imports.

"Imports into deficit regions would put pressure on the higher market prices prevailing there and could compromise the regional premiums added to the intervention and beet prices in the beet regions," he said.

Under the EU's current sugar regime, valid until June 2001, import tariffs provide a high level of protection. Stendevad said massive imports of cheap sugar could lead to EU sugar being offered to intervention and quota cuts could result if GATT ceilings on exports with refunds prevented this sugar from being exported.
